427	      "goal": "Tell the Lava Mouth origin story in a way that makes the brand feel human, earned, and worth rooting for. This is the page that converts casual buyers into loyal fans. The scroll should feel like reading a great short story \u2014 deliberate, warm, and surprising.",
428	      "meta_description": "How a backyard obsession with peppers turned into Lava Mouth \u2014 the small-batch hot sauce brand built on flavor, fire, and stubbornness.",

433	          "intent": "Open the story with a cinematic, emotionally charged statement that signals this page is different \u2014 slower, more personal, worth reading. A deliberate stillness after the energy of the rest of the site.",
434	          "eyebrow": "The Origin",
435	          "headline": "It Started With a Pepper Plant and a Dare",

446	          "eyebrow": "Chapter One",
447	          "headline": "A Garden, a Blender, and a Very Unhappy Neighbor",
448	          "subheadline": null,
449	          "body": "In 2018, founder Dani Reyes planted a single row of ghost peppers in her Chicago apartment's community garden plot. By August, she had more peppers than she knew what to do with. By September, she had a blender, a dozen mason jars, and a sauce that her neighbors described as 'aggressively good' and 'slightly dangerous.' By December, she was selling out of a folding table at the Logan Square Farmers Market every Saturday. Nobody was more surprised than Dani.\n\nLava Mouth wasn't planned. It was grown. The early sauces were made in a rented commercial kitchen from midnight to 4am, labeled by hand at the kitchen table, and sold from the back of a hatchback. Every batch was an experiment. Most were brilliant. A few were spectacular failures that have been sworn to secrecy.\n\nThe name came from Dani's nephew, who tried the original ghost pepper sauce at age nine and announced \u2014 with tears streaming down his face \u2014 that his mouth felt like lava. He asked for more. The name stuck.",

513	          "headline": "Flavor First. Heat Second. Always Small-Batch.",
514	          "subheadline": null,
515	          "body": "A lot of hot sauce brands are in the business of pain. We're in the business of flavor. The heat is real \u2014 sometimes brutally so \u2014 but every Lava Mouth sauce is built around a flavor profile first. The pepper comes second. That's the rule Dani set in 2018 and it hasn't changed.\n\nSmall-batch isn't a marketing phrase for us. It's a hard cap. Every run is 500 bottles or fewer. The page moves through five distinct emotional beats: (1) an explosive hero that announces the brand personality before a single scroll, (2) a bold three-pillar brand statement with graphic icon cards, (3) a collectible product showcase, (4) a typographic stat moment that earns credibility, and (5) a celebratory closing CTA that makes not buying feel like a mistake. Each section has a different skeleton — no two sections share the same layout DNA — so the scroll feels like turning pages in a zine rather than advancing through a template.

### Section Rhythm & Skeleton Variety
- **Section 1 (Hero):** Full-bleed, asymmetric, illustration-dominant. Off-center type stack pushed left, mascot illustration overflowing the right edge and bleeding into the section below. Memphis shapes scatter across the full surface.
- **Section 2 (Feature Grid):** Habanero Yellow full-bleed panel. Three cards in a horizontal row with staggered vertical offsets — the middle card pushed up, the outer two sitting lower — breaking the flat grid. Icons sit large and centered above each card's copy.
- **Section 3 (Product Grid):** Lava Cream surface, four product cards in a 2×2 grid at wide viewport (scrolling 2-up at mobile). Each card is a bold color block with a distinct palette assignment — no two cards share the same background color. Cards feel like collectible label peels.
- **Section 4 (Stats):** Ghost Pepper Purple full-bleed panel. Stats rendered as massive Boogaloo numerals — oversized to the point of being typographic objects, not just data. This is the page's **signature moment** (see below).
- **Section 5 (CTA Close):** Molten Coral full-bleed. Centered composition (justified by the celebratory, punchy close energy). Confetti shapes rain across the surface. Two CTAs side by side.

### Signature Moment
**Section 4 — "Oversized Numeral Eruption on Ghost Pepper Purple."** The four stats are rendered as enormous Boogaloo numerals — each number at 120–160px, filling its column to near-overflow — printed in alternating Habanero Yellow and Molten Coral directly on the Ghost Pepper Purple panel. The labels beneath each number are tiny Permanent Marker in Lava Cream, creating a violent scale contrast that makes the numbers feel like graffiti stencils on a wall. This is unmistakably Memphis: bold graphic type used as image, flat color doing all the heavy lifting, zero decoration needed because the type IS the decoration. The numbers count up from zero as the section enters the viewport — a scroll-triggered counting animation — making the arrival of each stat feel like a small celebration.

**Signature Motion Moment:** As Section 4 scrolls into view, each of the four oversized numerals counts up from 0 to its final value in a staggered sequence — the first number starts counting, then a beat later the second joins, then the third, then the fourth — so the purple panel feels like it's erupting with data. The counting motion is fast and snappy (each number reaches its final value in about one second), and when each number lands, it gives a brief elastic bounce — scaling up slightly past its final size then settling back — echoing the Memphis energy of the whole page.

### Color & Surface Logic Across the Page
- Section 1: Lava Cream background with Molten Coral headline fill, Ghost Pepper Purple for the eyebrow pill, Confetti Pink and Habanero Yellow Memphis shapes scattered across the surface.
- Section 2: Habanero Yellow full-bleed background. Cards are Lava Cream with Smoke Ring Black text and Molten Coral icon fills.
- Section 3: Lava Cream background. Product card backgrounds cycle: Molten Coral, Jalapeño Teal, Ghost Pepper Purple, Sauce Bottle Green — each card is a saturated block with Lava Cream or white text.
- Section 4: Ghost Pepper Purple full-bleed. Numerals in alternating Habanero Yellow and Molten Coral. Label text in Lava Cream via Permanent Marker.
- Section 5: Molten Coral full-bleed. Headline in Habanero Yellow. Subhead in Lava Cream. CTAs: one Ghost Pepper Purple fill with Lava Cream text, one Lava Cream fill with Smoke Ring Black text.

### Typographic Hierarchy
- H1 (Hero): Boogaloo, 88–100px, all-caps, Molten Coral fill on Lava Cream. Tight tracking. Feels shouted.
- H2 (Section headlines): Boogaloo, 52–64px, sentence case except Section 5 which is all-caps. Color varies by section surface.
- H3 (Card/item titles): Boogaloo, 36–40px, sentence case.
- Eyebrow labels: Permanent Marker, 12–14px, loose tracking, in pill backgrounds.
- Body / descriptions: Nunito, 16–18px, 1.7 line-height, 400 weight for card descriptions, 600 semi-bold for section subheadlines.
- Stat numerals (Section 4): Boogaloo, 120–160px, treated as graphic objects.

### Memphis Visual Cues — Applied at Full Amplitude
Memphis shapes are NOT tucked into corners. In the hero, abstract squiggles, zigzag lines, confetti triangles, and dot clusters are scattered across the full surface at varying scales — some behind the headline, some overlapping the mascot illustration's edges, some bleeding off the viewport edge. In Section 5, confetti shapes (triangles, circles, squiggles) fall across the coral panel at multiple depths, some at 60% opacity to create layering. The mascot illustration in the hero overflows its container, crossing into the section below — a deliberate Memphis overlap that refuses to stay inside its box.

### Density & Whitespace Logic
The page alternates between dense/graphic sections (Hero, Stats, CTA Close) and slightly more breathable sections (Feature Grid cards, Product Grid cards). Even the "breathable" sections are energetic — the breathing room is used for bold color blocks, not empty space. No section feels like a rest; each feels like a different flavor of loud.

### Motion Design — Full Arc

**On-Load Arc (Hero):**
1. The Habanero Yellow and Confetti Pink Memphis background shapes fade and slide in from slightly off-position simultaneously as the page loads — a quick 300ms scatter-settle.
2. A beat after the shapes settle, the eyebrow pill pops in with a quick scale-from-zero bounce.
3. The H1 headline slams in from slightly below — a fast upward slide with a tiny elastic overshoot — landing hard like a stamp.
4. A beat after the headline lands, the subheadline fades up from below.
5. A beat after the subhead, the two CTA buttons slide in from the left with a short stagger between them.
6. The mascot illustration drifts in from the right edge — a smooth slide-in that arrives slightly after the CTAs — and then begins a slow, continuous ambient float (gentle up-down drift on a 4-second loop, very subtle, as if the chili is breathing).
7. The Memphis background shapes continue a very slow, almost imperceptible parallax drift as the user scrolls — shapes in the "foreground" move slightly faster than those in the "background."

**Scroll-Triggered Reveals:**
- Section 2 (Feature Grid): The section headline slides up and fades in as the section enters the viewport. The three cards stagger in from below — left card first, then center (which is also pushed up vertically), then right — each with a quick upward slide and fade, arriving about half a beat apart.
- Section 3 (Product Grid): Cards scale in from 95% to 100% with a fade, staggered in reading order (top-left → top-right → bottom-left → bottom-right), each arriving a beat after the previous.
- Section 4 (Stats): The Ghost Pepper Purple panel fades in as a full-bleed color wash, then the four stat numerals count up from zero in a staggered sequence — first number starts, then a beat later the second joins, and so on. Each number lands with a brief elastic bounce. This is the **signature motion moment**.
- Section 5 (CTA Close): The confetti shapes scatter across the coral panel as it enters the viewport — a quick burst-and-settle. The headline scales up from 90% with a fade. CTAs slide up staggered.

**Hover & Focus Affordances:**
- Hero CTAs: On hover, the primary CTA (Shop the Sauces) lifts 4px with a shadow deepening and its background shifts one shade darker (coral darkens). The secondary CTA border brightens. Both respond to keyboard focus with a visible outline in Habanero Yellow.
- Feature Grid cards: On hover, the card lifts 6px, shadow grows, and the icon scales up to 110% with a quick 150ms ease. The card border (Smoke Ring Black, 2px) thickens to 3px.
- Product cards: On hover, the card scales to 102%, the product title shifts to Habanero Yellow (on dark card backgrounds) or Molten Coral (on light ones), and a "View Sauce →" text link fades in at the bottom of the card.
- CTA Close buttons: On hover, the Ghost Pepper Purple button gains a Habanero Yellow border and the text shifts to Habanero Yellow. The Lava Cream button gains a Smoke Ring Black border.
- All interactive elements have a visible focus ring in Habanero Yellow for keyboard navigation.

**Ambient Looped Motion:**
- Hero mascot illustration: slow, continuous up-down float on a 4-second loop.
- Memphis background shapes in the hero: extremely slow rotation drift (some shapes rotate 1–2 degrees over 8 seconds and back) — barely perceptible but adds life.
- Section 5 CTA close: the primary "Shop Now" button has a slow pulsing glow — a soft Habanero Yellow halo that breathes in and out on a 2.5-second loop — making it feel like it's beckoning.
- A marquee strip between Section 2 and Section 3: a continuous left-scrolling ticker of alternating sauce names and flame emoji, rendered in Boogaloo on a Jalapeño Teal strip — scrolls at a steady, hypnotic pace. This is a structural Memphis device, not decoration.

### Responsive Behavior
- **Desktop (1280px+):** All layouts as described. Hero is full-viewport-height. Product grid is 2×2. Stats are four columns.
- **Tablet (768–1279px):** Hero text stack and mascot stack vertically (text above, illustration below, still overflowing). Feature grid becomes a 3-column row but cards are narrower. Product grid stays 2×2. Stats become 2×2.
- **Mobile (< 768px):** Hero is single-column, mascot illustration sits below the text stack and is cropped to show the face/upper body only. Feature grid stacks to a single column. Product grid stacks to a single column with full-width cards. Stats stack 2×2. CTA close stacks CTAs vertically. Marquee strip persists at all breakpoints. Memphis shapes scale down but remain visible — never hidden.

### Fit Within Shared Design System
This page uses all eight palette colors expressively — not just as accent touches. Boogaloo dominates at display scale. Nunito handles all body copy. Permanent Marker appears on eyebrow pills and stat labels only — never at heading scale. The mascot illustration and Memphis icon set introduced here establish visual motifs that echo across the Products and Story pages. The marquee strip device will recur on the Products page, creating cross-page rhythm.",

### Page Role & Narrative Arc
The Home page is the brand's loudest arrival moment — a kinetic, Memphis-saturated scroll that hits like a street-market stall and never lets up. The page moves through five distinct emotional beats: (1) an explosive hero that announces the brand personality before a single scroll, (2) a bold three-pillar brand statement with graphic icon cards, (3) a collectible product showcase, (4) a typographic stat moment that earns credibility, and (5) a celebratory closing CTA that makes not buying feel like a mistake. Each section has a different skeleton — no two sections share the same layout DNA — so the scroll feels like turning pages in a zine rather than advancing through a template.

### Section Rhythm & Skeleton Variety
- **Section 1 (Hero):** Full-bleed, asymmetric, illustration-dominant. Off-center type stack pushed left, mascot illustration overflowing the right edge and bleeding into the section below. Memphis shapes scatter across the full surface.
- **Section 2 (Feature Grid):** Habanero Yellow full-bleed panel. Three cards in a horizontal row with staggered vertical offsets — the middle card pushed up, the outer two sitting lower — breaking the flat grid. Icons sit large and centered above each card's copy.
- **Section 3 (Product Grid):** Lava Cream surface, four product cards in a 2×2 grid at wide viewport (scrolling 2-up at mobile). Each card is a bold color block with a distinct palette assignment — no two cards share the same background color. Cards feel like collectible label peels.
- **Section 4 (Stats):** Ghost Pepper Purple full-bleed panel. Stats rendered as massive Boogaloo numerals — oversized to the point of being typographic objects, not just data. This is the page's **signature moment** (see below).
- **Section 5 (CTA Close):** Molten Coral full-bleed. Centered composition (justified by the celebratory, punchy close energy). Confetti shapes rain across the surface. Two CTAs side by side.

### Signature Moment
**Section 4 — "Oversized Numeral Eruption on Ghost Pepper Purple."** The four stats are rendered as enormous Boogaloo numerals — each number at 120–160px, filling its column to near-overflow — printed in alternating Habanero Yellow and Molten Coral directly on the Ghost Pepper Purple panel. The labels beneath each number are tiny Permanent Marker in Lava Cream, creating a violent scale contrast that makes the numbers feel like graffiti stencils on a wall. This is unmistakably Memphis: bold graphic type used as image, flat color doing all the heavy lifting, zero decoration needed because the type IS the decoration. The numbers count up from zero as the section enters the viewport — a scroll-triggered counting animation — making the arrival of each stat feel like a small celebration.

**Signature Motion Moment:** As Section 4 scrolls into view, each of the four oversized numerals counts up from 0 to its final value in a staggered sequence — the first number starts counting, then a beat later the second joins, then the third, then the fourth — so the purple panel feels like it's erupting with data. The counting motion is fast and snappy (each number reaches its final value in about one second), and when each number lands, it gives a brief elastic bounce — scaling up slightly past its final size then settling back — echoing the Memphis energy of the whole page.

### Color & Surface Logic Across the Page
- Section 1: Lava Cream background with Molten Coral headline fill, Ghost Pepper Purple for the eyebrow pill, Confetti Pink and Habanero Yellow Memphis shapes scattered across the surface.
- Section 2: Habanero Yellow full-bleed background. Cards are Lava Cream with Smoke Ring Black text and Molten Coral icon fills.
- Section 3: Lava Cream background. Product card backgrounds cycle: Molten Coral, Jalapeño Teal, Ghost Pepper Purple, Sauce Bottle Green — each card is a saturated block with Lava Cream or white text.
- Section 4: Ghost Pepper Purple full-bleed. Numerals in alternating Habanero Yellow and Molten Coral. Label text in Lava Cream via Permanent Marker.
- Section 5: Molten Coral full-bleed. Headline in Habanero Yellow. Subhead in Lava Cream. CTAs: one Ghost Pepper Purple fill with Lava Cream text, one Lava Cream fill with Smoke Ring Black text.

### Typographic Hierarchy
- H1 (Hero): Boogaloo, 88–100px, all-caps, Molten Coral fill on Lava Cream. Tight tracking. Feels shouted.
- H2 (Section headlines): Boogaloo, 52–64px, sentence case except Section 5 which is all-caps. Color varies by section surface.
- H3 (Card/item titles): Boogaloo, 36–40px, sentence case.
- Eyebrow labels: Permanent Marker, 12–14px, loose tracking, in pill backgrounds.
- Body / descriptions: Nunito, 16–18px, 1.7 line-height, 400 weight for card descriptions, 600 semi-bold for section subheadlines.
- Stat numerals (Section 4): Boogaloo, 120–160px, treated as graphic objects.

### Memphis Visual Cues — Applied at Full Amplitude
Memphis shapes are NOT tucked into corners. In the hero, abstract squiggles, zigzag lines, confetti triangles, and dot clusters are scattered across the full surface at varying scales — some behind the headline, some overlapping the mascot illustration's edges, some bleeding off the viewport edge. In Section 5, confetti shapes (triangles, circles, squiggles) fall across the coral panel at multiple depths, some at 60% opacity to create layering. The mascot illustration in the hero overflows its container, crossing into the section below — a deliberate Memphis overlap that refuses to stay inside its box.

### Density & Whitespace Logic
The page alternates between dense/graphic sections (Hero, Stats, CTA Close) and slightly more breathable sections (Feature Grid cards, Product Grid cards). Even the "breathable" sections are energetic — the breathing room is used for bold color blocks, not empty space. No section feels like a rest; each feels like a different flavor of loud.

### Motion Design — Full Arc

**On-Load Arc (Hero):**
1. The Habanero Yellow and Confetti Pink Memphis background shapes fade and slide in from slightly off-position simultaneously as the page loads — a quick 300ms scatter-settle.
2. A beat after the shapes settle, the eyebrow pill pops in with a quick scale-from-zero bounce.
3. The H1 headline slams in from slightly below — a fast upward slide with a tiny elastic overshoot — landing hard like a stamp.
4. A beat after the headline lands, the subheadline fades up from below.
5. A beat after the subhead, the two CTA buttons slide in from the left with a short stagger between them.

**Ambient Looped Motion:**
- Hero mascot illustration: slow, continuous up-down float on a 4-second loop.
- Memphis background shapes in the hero: extremely slow rotation drift (some shapes rotate 1–2 degrees over 8 seconds and back) — barely perceptible but adds life.
- Section 5 CTA close: the primary "Shop Now" button has a slow pulsing glow — a soft Habanero Yellow halo that breathes in and out on a 2.5-second loop — making it feel like it's beckoning.
- A marquee strip between Section 2 and Section 3: a continuous left-scrolling ticker of alternating sauce names and flame emoji, rendered in Boogaloo on a Jalapeño Teal strip — scrolls at a steady, hypnotic pace. This is a structural Memphis device, not decoration.

### Responsive Behavior
- **Desktop (1280px+):** All layouts as described. Hero is full-viewport-height. Product grid is 2×2. Stats are four columns.

Memphis shapes scale down but remain visible — never hidden.

PAGE INSTR:
## Home Page — Lava Mouth Visual Design Plan

### Page Role & Narrative Arc
The Home page is the brand's loudest arrival moment — a kinetic, Memphis-saturated scroll that hits like a street-market stall and never lets up. The page moves through five distinct emotional beats: (1) an explosive hero that announces the brand personality before a single scroll, (2) a bold three-pillar brand statement with graphic icon cards, (3) a collectible product showcase, (4) a typographic stat moment that earns credibility, and (5) a celebratory closing CTA that makes not buying feel like a mistake. Each section has a different skeleton — no two sections share the same layout DNA — so the scroll feels like turning pages in a zine rather than advancing through a template.

### Section Rhythm & Skeleton Variety
- **Section 1 (Hero):** Full-bleed, asymmetric, illustration-dominant. Off-center type stack pushed left, mascot illustration overflowing the right edge and bleeding into the section below. Memphis shapes scatter across the full surface.
- **Section 2 (Feature Grid):** Habanero Yellow full-bleed panel. Three cards in a horizontal row with staggered vertical offsets — the middle card pushed up, the outer two sitting lower — breaking the flat grid. Icons sit large and centered above each card's copy.
- **Section 3 (Product Grid):** Lava Cream surface, four product cards in a 2×2 grid at wide viewport (scrolling 2-up at mobile). Each card is a bold color block with a distinct palette assignment — no two cards share the same background color. Cards feel like collectible label peels.
- **Section 4 (Stats):** Ghost Pepper Purple full-bleed panel. Stats rendered as massive Boogaloo numerals — oversized to the point of being typographic objects, not just data. This is the page's **signature moment** (see below).
- **Section 5 (CTA Close):** Molten Coral full-bleed. Centered composition (justified by the celebratory, punchy close energy). Confetti shapes rain across the surface. Two CTAs side by side.

### Signature Moment
**Section 4 — "Oversized Numeral Eruption on Ghost Pepper Purple."** The four stats are rendered as enormous Boogaloo numerals — each number at 120–160px, filling its column to near-overflow — printed in alternating Habanero Yellow and Molten Coral directly on the Ghost Pepper Purple panel. The labels beneath each number are tiny Permanent Marker in Lava Cream, creating a violent scale contrast that makes the numbers feel like graffiti stencils on a wall. This is unmistakably Memphis: bold graphic type used as image, flat color doing all the heavy lifting, zero decoration needed because the type IS the decoration. The numbers count up from zero as the section enters the viewport — a scroll-triggered counting animation — making the arrival of each stat feel like a small celebration.

**Signature Motion Moment:** As Section 4 scrolls into view, each of the four oversized numerals counts up from 0 to its final value in a staggered sequence — the first number starts counting, then a beat later the second joins, then the third, then the fourth — so the purple panel feels like it's erupting with data. The counting motion is fast and snappy (each number reaches its final value in about one second), and when each number lands, it gives a brief elastic bounce — scaling up slightly past its final size then settling back — echoing the Memphis energy of the whole page.

### Color & Surface Logic Across the Page
- Section 1: Lava Cream background with Molten Coral headline fill, Ghost Pepper Purple for the eyebrow pill, Confetti Pink and Habanero Yellow Memphis shapes scattered across the surface.
- Section 2: Habanero Yellow full-bleed background. Cards are Lava Cream with Smoke Ring Black text and Molten Coral icon fills.
- Section 3: Lava Cream background. Product card backgrounds cycle: Molten Coral, Jalapeño Teal, Ghost Pepper Purple, Sauce Bottle Green — each card is a saturated block with Lava Cream or white text.
- Section 4: Ghost Pepper Purple full-bleed. Numerals in alternating Habanero Yellow and Molten Coral. Label text in Lava Cream via Permanent Marker.
- Section 5: Molten Coral full-bleed. Headline in Habanero Yellow. Subhead in Lava Cream. CTAs: one Ghost Pepper Purple fill with Lava Cream text, one Lava Cream fill with Smoke Ring Black text.

### Typographic Hierarchy
- H1 (Hero): Boogaloo, 88–100px, all-caps, Molten Coral fill on Lava Cream. Tight tracking. Feels shouted.
- H2 (Section headlines): Boogaloo, 52–64px, sentence case except Section 5 which is all-caps. Color varies by section surface.
- H3 (Card/item titles): Boogaloo, 36–40px, sentence case.
- Eyebrow labels: Permanent Marker, 12–14px, loose tracking, in pill backgrounds.
- Body / descriptions: Nunito, 16–18px, 1.7 line-height, 400 weight for card descriptions, 600 semi-bold for section subheadlines.
- Stat numerals (Section 4): Boogaloo, 120–160px, treated as graphic objects.

### Memphis Visual Cues — Applied at Full Amplitude
Memphis shapes are NOT tucked into corners. In the hero, abstract squiggles, zigzag lines, confetti triangles, and dot clusters are scattered across the full surface at varying scales — some behind the headline, some overlapping the mascot illustration's edges, some bleeding off the viewport edge. In Section 5, confetti shapes (triangles, circles, squiggles) fall across the coral panel at multiple depths, some at 60% opacity to create layering. The mascot illustration in the hero overflows its container, crossing into the section below — a deliberate Memphis overlap that refuses to stay inside its box.

### Density & Whitespace Logic
The page alternates between dense/graphic sections (Hero, Stats, CTA Close) and slightly more breathable sections (Feature Grid cards, Product Grid cards). Even the "breathable" sections are energetic — the breathing room is used for bold color blocks, not empty space. No section feels like a rest; each feels like a different flavor of loud.

### Motion Design — Full Arc

**On-Load Arc (Hero):**
1. The Habanero Yellow and Confetti Pink Memphis background shapes fade and slide in from slightly off-position simultaneously as the page loads — a quick 300ms scatter-settle.
2. A beat after the shapes settle, the eyebrow pill pops in with a quick scale-from-zero bounce.
3. The H1 headline slams in from slightly below — a fast upward slide with a tiny elastic overshoot — landing hard like a stamp.
4. A beat after the headline lands, the subheadline fades up from below.
5. A beat after the subhead, the two CTA buttons slide in from the left with a short stagger between them.
6. The mascot illustration drifts in from the right edge — a smooth slide-in that arrives slightly after the CTAs — and then begins a slow, continuous ambient float (gentle up-down drift on a 4-second loop, very subtle, as if the chili is breathing).
7. The Memphis background shapes continue a very slow, almost imperceptible parallax drift as the user scrolls — shapes in the "foreground" move slightly faster than those in the "background."

**Scroll-Triggered Reveals:**
- Section 2 (Feature Grid): The section headline slides up and fades in as the section enters the viewport. The three cards stagger in from below — left card first, then center (which is also pushed up vertically), then right — each with a quick upward slide and fade, arriving about half a beat apart.
- Section 3 (Product Grid): Cards scale in from 95% to 100% with a fade, staggered in reading order (top-left → top-right → bottom-left → bottom-right), each arriving a beat after the previous.
- Section 4 (Stats): The Ghost Pepper Purple panel fades in as a full-bleed color wash, then the four stat numerals count up from zero in a staggered sequence — first number starts, then a beat later the second joins, and so on. Each number lands with a brief elastic bounce. This is the **signature motion moment**.
- Section 5 (CTA Close): The confetti shapes scatter across the coral panel as it enters the viewport — a quick burst-and-settle. The headline scales up from 90% with a fade. CTAs slide up staggered.

**Hover & Focus Affordances:**
- Hero CTAs: On hover, the primary CTA (Shop the Sauces) lifts 4px with a shadow deepening and its background shifts one shade darker (coral darkens). The secondary CTA border brightens. Both respond to keyboard focus with a visible outline in Habanero Yellow.
- Feature Grid cards: On hover, the card lifts 6px, shadow grows, and the icon scales up to 110% with a quick 150ms ease. The card border (Smoke Ring Black, 2px) thickens to 3px.
- Product cards: On hover, the card scales to 102%, the product title shifts to Habanero Yellow (on dark card backgrounds) or Molten Coral (on light ones), and a "View Sauce →" text link fades in at the bottom of the card.
- CTA Close buttons: On hover, the Ghost Pepper Purple button gains a Habanero Yellow border and the text shifts to Habanero Yellow. The Lava Cream button gains a Smoke Ring Black border.
- All interactive elements have a visible focus ring in Habanero Yellow for keyboard navigation.

**Ambient Looped Motion:**
- Hero mascot illustration: slow, continuous up-down float on a 4-second loop.
- Memphis background shapes in the hero: extremely slow rotation drift (some shapes rotate 1–2 degrees over 8 seconds and back) — barely perceptible but adds life.
- Section 5 CTA close: the primary "Shop Now" button has a slow pulsing glow — a soft Habanero Yellow halo that breathes in and out on a 2.5-second loop — making it feel like it's beckoning.
- A marquee strip between Section 2 and Section 3: a continuous left-scrolling ticker of alternating sauce names and flame emoji, rendered in Boogaloo on a Jalapeño Teal strip — scrolls at a steady, hypnotic pace. This is a structural Memphis device, not decoration.

### Responsive Behavior
- **Desktop (1280px+):** All layouts as described. Hero is full-viewport-height. Product grid is 2×2. Stats are four columns.
- **Tablet (768–1279px):** Hero text stack and mascot stack vertically (text above, illustration below, still overflowing). Feature grid becomes a 3-column row but cards are narrower. Product grid stays 2×2. Stats become 2×2.
- **Mobile (< 768px):** Hero is single-column, mascot illustration sits below the text stack and is cropped to show the face/upper body only. Feature grid stacks to a single column. Product grid stacks to a single column with full-width cards. Stats stack 2×2. CTA close stacks CTAs vertically. Marquee strip persists at all breakpoints. Memphis shapes scale down but remain visible — never hidden.

### Fit Within Shared Design System
This page uses all eight palette colors expressively — not just as accent touches. Boogaloo dominates at display scale. Nunito handles all body copy. Permanent Marker appears on eyebrow pills and stat labels only — never at heading scale. The mascot illustration and Memphis icon set introduced here establish visual motifs that echo across the Products and Story pages. The marquee strip device will recur on the Products page, creating cross-page rhythm.
---

PAGE INSTR:
## Home Page — Lava Mouth Visual Design Plan

### Page Role & Narrative Arc
The Home page is the brand's loudest arrival moment — a kinetic, Memphis-saturated scroll that hits like a street-market stall and never lets up. The page moves through five distinct emotional beats: (1) an explosive hero that announces the brand personality before a single scroll, (2) a bold three-pillar brand statement with graphic icon cards, (3) a collectible product showcase, (4) a typographic stat moment that earns credibility, and (5) a celebratory closing CTA that makes not buying feel like a mistake. Each section has a different skeleton — no two sections share the same layout DNA — so the scroll feels like turning pages in a zine rather than advancing through a template.

### Section Rhythm & Skeleton Variety
- **Section 1 (Hero):** Full-bleed, asymmetric, illustration-dominant. Off-center type stack pushed left, mascot illustration overflowing the right edge and bleeding into the section below. Memphis shapes scatter across the full surface.
- **Section 2 (Feature Grid):** Habanero Yellow full-bleed panel. Three cards in a horizontal row with staggered vertical offsets — the middle card pushed up, the outer two sitting lower — breaking the flat grid. Icons sit large and centered above each card's copy.
- **Section 3 (Product Grid):** Lava Cream surface, four product cards in a 2×2 grid at wide viewport (scrolling 2-up at mobile). Each card is a bold color block with a distinct palette assignment — no two cards share the same background color. Cards feel like collectible label peels.
- **Section 4 (Stats):** Ghost Pepper Purple full-bleed panel. Stats rendered as massive Boogaloo numerals — oversized to the point of being typographic objects, not just data. This is the page's **signature moment** (see below).
- **Section 5 (CTA Close):** Molten Coral full-bleed. Centered composition (justified by the celebratory, punchy close energy). Confetti shapes rain across the surface. Two CTAs side by side.

### Signature Moment
**Section 4 — "Oversized Numeral Eruption on Ghost Pepper Purple."** The four stats are rendered as enormous Boogaloo numerals — each number at 120–160px, filling its column to near-overflow — printed in alternating Habanero Yellow and Molten Coral directly on the Ghost Pepper Purple panel. The labels beneath each number are tiny Permanent Marker in Lava Cream, creating a violent scale contrast that makes the numbers feel like graffiti stencils on a wall. This is unmistakably Memphis: bold graphic type used as image, flat color doing all the heavy lifting, zero decoration needed because the type IS the decoration. The numbers count up from zero as the section enters the viewport — a scroll-triggered counting animation — making the arrival of each stat feel like a small celebration.

**Signature Motion Moment:** As Section 4 scrolls into view, each of the four oversized numerals counts up from 0 to its final value in a staggered sequence — the first number starts counting, then a beat later the second joins, then the third, then the fourth — so the purple panel feels like it's erupting with data. The counting motion is fast and snappy (each number reaches its final value in about one second), and when each number lands, it gives a brief elastic bounce — scaling up slightly past its final size then settling back — echoing the Memphis energy of the whole page.

### Color & Surface Logic Across the Page
- Section 1: Lava Cream background with Molten Coral headline fill, Ghost Pepper Purple for the eyebrow pill, Confetti Pink and Habanero Yellow Memphis shapes scattered across the surface.
- Section 2: Habanero Yellow full-bleed background. Cards are Lava Cream with Smoke Ring Black text and Molten Coral icon fills.
- Section 3: Lava Cream background. Product card backgrounds cycle: Molten Coral, Jalapeño Teal, Ghost Pepper Purple, Sauce Bottle Green — each card is a saturated block with Lava Cream or white text.
- Section 4: Ghost Pepper Purple full-bleed. Numerals in alternating Habanero Yellow and Molten Coral. Label text in Lava Cream via Permanent Marker.
- Section 5: Molten Coral full-bleed. Headline in Habanero Yellow. Subhead in Lava Cream. CTAs: one Ghost Pepper Purple fill with Lava Cream text, one Lava Cream fill with Smoke Ring Black text.

### Typographic Hierarchy
- H1 (Hero): Boogaloo, 88–100px, all-caps, Molten Coral fill on Lava Cream. Tight tracking. Feels shouted.
- H2 (Section headlines): Boogaloo, 52–64px, sentence case except Section 5 which is all-caps. Color varies by section surface.
- H3 (Card/item titles): Boogaloo, 36–40px, sentence case.
- Eyebrow labels: Permanent Marker, 12–14px, loose tracking, in pill backgrounds.
- Body / descriptions: Nunito, 16–18px, 1.7 line-height, 400 weight for card descriptions, 600 semi-bold for section subheadlines.
- Stat numerals (Section 4): Boogaloo, 120–160px, treated as graphic objects.

### Memphis Visual Cues — Applied at Full Amplitude
Memphis shapes are NOT tucked into corners. In the hero, abstract squiggles, zigzag lines, confetti triangles, and dot clusters are scattered across the full surface at varying scales — some behind the headline, some overlapping the mascot illustration's edges, some bleeding off the viewport edge. In Section 5, confetti shapes (triangles, circles, squiggles) fall across the coral panel at multiple depths, some at 60% opacity to create layering. The mascot illustration in the hero overflows its container, crossing into the section below — a deliberate Memphis overlap that refuses to stay inside its box.

### Density & Whitespace Logic
The page alternates between dense/graphic sections (Hero, Stats, CTA Close) and slightly more breathable sections (Feature Grid cards, Product Grid cards). Even the "breathable" sections are energetic — the breathing room is used for bold color blocks, not empty space. No section feels like a rest; each feels like a different flavor of loud.

### Motion Design — Full Arc

**On-Load Arc (Hero):**
1. The Habanero Yellow and Confetti Pink Memphis background shapes fade and slide in from slightly off-position simultaneously as the page loads — a quick 300ms scatter-settle.
2. A beat after the shapes settle, the eyebrow pill pops in with a quick scale-from-zero bounce.
3. The H1 headline slams in from slightly below — a fast upward slide with a tiny elastic overshoot — landing hard like a stamp.
4. A beat after the headline lands, the subheadline fades up from below.
5. A beat after the subhead, the two CTA buttons slide in from the left with a short stagger between them.
6. The mascot illustration drifts in from the right edge — a smooth slide-in that arrives slightly after the CTAs — and then begins a slow, continuous ambient float (gentle up-down drift on a 4-second loop, very subtle, as if the chili is breathing).
7. The Memphis background shapes continue a very slow, almost imperceptible parallax drift as the user scrolls — shapes in the "foreground" move slightly faster than those in the "background."

**Scroll-Triggered Reveals:**
- Section 2 (Feature Grid): The section headline slides up and fades in as the section enters the viewport. The three cards stagger in from below — left card first, then center (which is also pushed up vertically), then right — each with a quick upward slide and fade, arriving about half a beat apart.
- Section 3 (Product Grid): Cards scale in from 95% to 100% with a fade, staggered in reading order (top-left → top-right → bottom-left → bottom-right), each arriving a beat after the previous.
- Section 4 (Stats): The Ghost Pepper Purple panel fades in as a full-bleed color wash, then the four stat numerals count up from zero in a staggered sequence — first number starts, then a beat later the second joins, and so on. Each number lands with a brief elastic bounce. This is the **signature motion moment**.
- Section 5 (CTA Close): The confetti shapes scatter across the coral panel as it enters the viewport — a quick burst-and-settle. The headline scales up from 90% with a fade. CTAs slide up staggered.

**Hover & Focus Affordances:**
- Hero CTAs: On hover, the primary CTA (Shop the Sauces) lifts 4px with a shadow deepening and its background shifts one shade darker (coral darkens). The secondary CTA border brightens. Both respond to keyboard focus with a visible outline in Habanero Yellow.
- Feature Grid cards: On hover, the card lifts 6px, shadow grows, and the icon scales up to 110% with a quick 150ms ease. The card border (Smoke Ring Black, 2px) thickens to 3px.
- Product cards: On hover, the card scales to 102%, the product title shifts to Habanero Yellow (on dark card backgrounds) or Molten Coral (on light ones), and a "View Sauce →" text link fades in at the bottom of the card.
- CTA Close buttons: On hover, the Ghost Pepper Purple button gains a Habanero Yellow border and the text shifts to Habanero Yellow. The Lava Cream button gains a Smoke Ring Black border.
- All interactive elements have a visible focus ring in Habanero Yellow for keyboard navigation.

**Ambient Looped Motion:**
- Hero mascot illustration: slow, continuous up-down float on a 4-second loop.
- Memphis background shapes in the hero: extremely slow rotation drift (some shapes rotate 1–2 degrees over 8 seconds and back) — barely perceptible but adds life.
- Section 5 CTA close: the primary "Shop Now" button has a slow pulsing glow — a soft Habanero Yellow halo that breathes in and out on a 2.5-second loop — making it feel like it's beckoning.
- A marquee strip between Section 2 and Section 3: a continuous left-scrolling ticker of alternating sauce names and flame emoji, rendered in Boogaloo on a Jalapeño Teal strip — scrolls at a steady, hypnotic pace. This is a structural Memphis device, not decoration.

### Responsive Behavior
- **Desktop (1280px+):** All layouts as described. Hero is full-viewport-height. Product grid is 2×2. Stats are four columns.
- **Tablet (768–1279px):** Hero text stack and mascot stack vertically (text above, illustration below, still overflowing). Feature grid becomes a 3-column row but cards are narrower. Product grid stays 2×2. Stats become 2×2.
- **Mobile (< 768px):** Hero is single-column, mascot illustration sits below the text stack and is cropped to show the face/upper body only. Feature grid stacks to a single column. Product grid stacks to a single column with full-width cards. Stats stack 2×2. CTA close stacks CTAs vertically. Marquee strip persists at all breakpoints. Memphis shapes scale down but remain visible — never hidden.

### Fit Within Shared Design System
This page uses all eight palette colors expressively — not just as accent touches. Boogaloo dominates at display scale. Nunito handles all body copy. Permanent Marker appears on eyebrow pills and stat labels only — never at heading scale. The mascot illustration and Memphis icon set introduced here establish visual motifs that echo across the Products and Story pages. The marquee strip device will recur on the Products page, creating cross-page rhythm.

1	PAGE INSTR:
2	## Home Page — Lava Mouth Visual Design Plan
3	
4	### Page Role & Narrative Arc
5	The Home page is the brand's loudest arrival moment — a kinetic, Memphis-saturated scroll that hits like a street-market stall and never lets up. The page moves through five distinct emotional beats: (1) an explosive hero that announces the brand personality before a single scroll, (2) a bold three-pillar brand statement with graphic icon cards, (3) a collectible product showcase, (4) a typographic stat moment that earns credibility, and (5) a celebratory closing CTA that makes not buying feel like a mistake. Each section has a different skeleton — no two sections share the same layout DNA — so the scroll feels like turning pages in a zine rather than advancing through a template.
6	
7	### Section Rhythm & Skeleton Variety
8	- **Section 1 (Hero):** Full-bleed, asymmetric, illustration-dominant. Off-center type stack pushed left, mascot illustration overflowing the right edge and bleeding into the section below. Memphis shapes scatter across the full surface.
9	- **Section 2 (Feature Grid):** Habanero Yellow full-bleed panel. Three cards in a horizontal row with staggered vertical offsets — the middle card pushed up, the outer two sitting lower — breaking the flat grid. Icons sit large and centered above each card's copy.
10	- **Section 3 (Product Grid):** Lava Cream surface, four product cards in a 2×2 grid at wide viewport (scrolling 2-up at mobile). Each card is a bold color block with a distinct palette assignment — no two cards share the same background color. Cards feel like collectible label peels.
11	- **Section 4 (Stats):** Ghost Pepper Purple full-bleed panel. Stats rendered as massive Boogaloo numerals — oversized to the point of being typographic objects, not just data. This is the page's **signature moment** (see below).
12	- **Section 5 (CTA Close):** Molten Coral full-bleed. Centered composition (justified by the celebratory, punchy close energy). Confetti shapes rain across the surface. Two CTAs side by side.
13	
14	### Signature Moment
15	**Section 4 — "Oversized Numeral Eruption on Ghost Pepper Purple."** The four stats are rendered as enormous Boogaloo numerals — each number at 120–160px, filling its column to near-overflow — printed in alternating Habanero Yellow and Molten Coral directly on the Ghost Pepper Purple panel. The labels beneath each number are tiny Permanent Marker in Lava Cream, creating a violent scale contrast that makes the numbers feel like graffiti stencils on a wall. This is unmistakably Memphis: bold graphic type used as image, flat color doing all the heavy lifting, zero decoration needed because the type IS the decoration. The numbers count up from zero as the section enters the viewport — a scroll-triggered counting animation — making the arrival of each stat feel like a small celebration.
16	
17	**Signature Motion Moment:** As Section 4 scrolls into view, each of the four oversized numerals counts up from 0 to its final value in a staggered sequence — the first number starts counting, then a beat later the second joins, then the third, then the fourth — so the purple panel feels like it's erupting with data. The counting motion is fast and snappy (each number reaches its final value in about one second), and when each number lands, it gives a brief elastic bounce — scaling up slightly past its final size then settling back — echoing the Memphis energy of the whole page.
18	
19	### Color & Surface Logic Across the Page
20	- Section 1: Lava Cream background with Molten Coral headline fill, Ghost Pepper Purple for the eyebrow pill, Confetti Pink and Habanero Yellow Memphis shapes scattered across the surface.
21	- Section 2: Habanero Yellow full-bleed background. Cards are Lava Cream with Smoke Ring Black text and Molten Coral icon fills.
22	- Section 3: Lava Cream background. Product card backgrounds cycle: Molten Coral, Jalapeño Teal, Ghost Pepper Purple, Sauce Bottle Green — each card is a saturated block with Lava Cream or white text.
23	- Section 4: Ghost Pepper Purple full-bleed. Numerals in alternating Habanero Yellow and Molten Coral. Label text in Lava Cream via Permanent Marker.
24	- Section 5: Molten Coral full-bleed. Headline in Habanero Yellow. Subhead in Lava Cream. CTAs: one Ghost Pepper Purple fill with Lava Cream text, one Lava Cream fill with Smoke Ring Black text.
25	
26	### Typographic Hierarchy
27	- H1 (Hero): Boogaloo, 88–100px, all-caps, Molten Coral fill on Lava Cream. Tight tracking. Feels shouted.
28	- H2 (Section headlines): Boogaloo, 52–64px, sentence case except Section 5 which is all-caps. Color varies by section surface.
29	- H3 (Card/item titles): Boogaloo, 36–40px, sentence case.
30	- Eyebrow labels: Permanent Marker, 12–14px, loose tracking, in pill backgrounds.
31	- Body / descriptions: Nunito, 16–18px, 1.7 line-height, 400 weight for card descriptions, 600 semi-bold for section subheadlines.
32	- Stat numerals (Section 4): Boogaloo, 120–160px, treated as graphic objects.
33	
34	### Memphis Visual Cues — Applied at Full Amplitude
35	Memphis shapes are NOT tucked into corners. In the hero, abstract squiggles, zigzag lines, confetti triangles, and dot clusters are scattered across the full surface at varying scales — some behind the headline, some overlapping the mascot illustration's edges, some bleeding off the viewport edge. In Section 5, confetti shapes (triangles, circles, squiggles) fall across the coral panel at multiple depths, some at 60% opacity to create layering. The mascot illustration in the hero overflows its container, crossing into the section below — a deliberate Memphis overlap that refuses to stay inside its box.
36	
37	### Density & Whitespace Logic
38	The page alternates between dense/graphic sections (Hero, Stats, CTA Close) and slightly more breathable sections (Feature Grid cards, Product Grid cards). Even the "breathable" sections are energetic — the breathing room is used for bold color blocks, not empty space. No section feels like a rest; each feels like a different flavor of loud.
39	
40	### Motion Design — Full Arc
41	
42	**On-Load Arc (Hero):**
43	1. The Habanero Yellow and Confetti Pink Memphis background shapes fade and slide in from slightly off-position simultaneously as the page loads — a quick 300ms scatter-settle.
44	2. A beat after the shapes settle, the eyebrow pill pops in with a quick scale-from-zero bounce.
45	3. The H1 headline slams in from slightly below — a fast upward slide with a tiny elastic overshoot — landing hard like a stamp.
46	4. A beat after the headline lands, the subheadline fades up from below.
47	5. A beat after the subhead, the two CTA buttons slide in from the left with a short stagger between them.
48	6. The mascot illustration drifts in from the right edge — a smooth slide-in that arrives slightly after the CTAs — and then begins a slow, continuous ambient float (gentle up-down drift on a 4-second loop, very subtle, as if the chili is breathing).
49	7. The Memphis background shapes continue a very slow, almost imperceptible parallax drift as the user scrolls — shapes in the "foreground" move slightly faster than those in the "background."
50	
51	**Scroll-Triggered Reveals:**
52	- Section 2 (Feature Grid): The section headline slides up and fades in as the section enters the viewport. The three cards stagger in from below — left card first, then center (which is also pushed up vertically), then right — each with a quick upward slide and fade, arriving about half a beat apart.
53	- Section 3 (Product Grid): Cards scale in from 95% to 100% with a fade, staggered in reading order (top-left → top-right → bottom-left → bottom-right), each arriving a beat after the previous.
54	- Section 4 (Stats): The Ghost Pepper Purple panel fades in as a full-bleed color wash, then the four stat numerals count up from zero in a staggered sequence — first number starts, then a beat later the second joins, and so on. Each number lands with a brief elastic bounce. This is the **signature motion moment**.
55	- Section 5 (CTA Close): The confetti shapes scatter across the coral panel as it enters the viewport — a quick burst-and-settle. The headline scales up from 90% with a fade. CTAs slide up staggered.
56	
57	**Hover & Focus Affordances:**
58	- Hero CTAs: On hover, the primary CTA (Shop the Sauces) lifts 4px with a shadow deepening and its background shifts one shade darker (coral darkens). The secondary CTA border brightens. Both respond to keyboard focus with a visible outline in Habanero Yellow.
59	- Feature Grid cards: On hover, the card lifts 6px, shadow grows, and the icon scales up to 110% with a quick 150ms ease. The card border (Smoke Ring Black, 2px) thickens to 3px.
60	- Product cards: On hover, the card scales to 102%, the product title shifts to Habanero Yellow (on dark card backgrounds) or Molten Coral (on light ones), and a "View Sauce →" text link fades in at the bottom of the card.
61	- CTA Close buttons: On hover, the Ghost Pepper Purple button gains a Habanero Yellow border and the text shifts to Habanero Yellow. The Lava Cream button gains a Smoke Ring Black border.
62	- All interactive elements have a visible focus ring in Habanero Yellow for keyboard navigation.
63	
64	**Ambient Looped Motion:**
65	- Hero mascot illustration: slow, continuous up-down float on a 4-second loop.
66	- Memphis background shapes in the hero: extremely slow rotation drift (some shapes rotate 1–2 degrees over 8 seconds and back) — barely perceptible but adds life.
67	- Section 5 CTA close: the primary "Shop Now" button has a slow pulsing glow — a soft Habanero Yellow halo that breathes in and out on a 2.5-second loop — making it feel like it's beckoning.
68	- A marquee strip between Section 2 and Section 3: a continuous left-scrolling ticker of alternating sauce names and flame emoji, rendered in Boogaloo on a Jalapeño Teal strip — scrolls at a steady, hypnotic pace. This is a structural Memphis device, not decoration.
69	
70	### Responsive Behavior
71	- **Desktop (1280px+):** All layouts as described. Hero is full-viewport-height. Product grid is 2×2. Stats are four columns.
72	- **Tablet (768–1279px):** Hero text stack and mascot stack vertically (text above, illustration below, still overflowing). Feature grid becomes a 3-column row but cards are narrower. Product grid stays 2×2. Stats become 2×2.
73	- **Mobile (< 768px):** Hero is single-column, mascot illustration sits below the text stack and is cropped to show the face/upper body only. Feature grid stacks to a single column. Product grid stacks to a single column with full-width cards. Stats stack 2×2. CTA close stacks CTAs vertically. Marquee strip persists at all breakpoints. Memphis shapes scale down but remain visible — never hidden.
74	
75	### Fit Within Shared Design System
76	This page uses all eight palette colors expressively — not just as accent touches. Boogaloo dominates at display scale. Nunito handles all body copy. Permanent Marker appears on eyebrow pills and stat labels only — never at heading scale. The mascot illustration and Memphis icon set introduced here establish visual motifs that echo across the Products and Story pages. The marquee strip device will recur on the Products page, creating cross-page rhythm.

PAGE INSTR:
## Home Page — Lava Mouth Visual Design Plan

### Page Role & Narrative Arc
The Home page is the brand's loudest arrival moment — a kinetic, Memphis-saturated scroll that hits like a street-market stall and never lets up. The page moves through five distinct emotional beats: (1) an explosive hero that announces the brand personality before a single scroll, (2) a bold three-pillar brand statement with graphic icon cards, (3) a collectible product showcase, (4) a typographic stat moment that earns credibility, and (5) a celebratory closing CTA that makes not buying feel like a mistake. Each section has a different skeleton — no two sections share the same layout DNA — so the scroll feels like turning pages in a zine rather than advancing through a template.

### Section Rhythm & Skeleton Variety
- **Section 1 (Hero):** Full-bleed, asymmetric, illustration-dominant. Off-center type stack pushed left, mascot illustration overflowing the right edge and bleeding into the section below. Memphis shapes scatter across the full surface.
- **Section 2 (Feature Grid):** Habanero Yellow full-bleed panel. Three cards in a horizontal row with staggered vertical offsets — the middle card pushed up, the outer two sitting lower — breaking the flat grid. Icons sit large and centered above each card's copy.
- **Section 3 (Product Grid):** Lava Cream surface, four product cards in a 2×2 grid at wide viewport (scrolling 2-up at mobile). Each card is a bold color block with a distinct palette assignment — no two cards share the same background color. Cards feel like collectible label peels.
- **Section 4 (Stats):** Ghost Pepper Purple full-bleed panel. Stats rendered as massive Boogaloo numerals — oversized to the point of being typographic objects, not just data. This is the page's **signature moment** (see below).
- **Section 5 (CTA Close):** Molten Coral full-bleed. Centered composition (justified by the celebratory, punchy close energy). Confetti shapes rain across the surface. Two CTAs side by side.

### Signature Moment
**Section 4 — "Oversized Numeral Eruption on Ghost Pepper Purple."** The four stats are rendered as enormous Boogaloo numerals — each number at 120–160px, filling its column to near-overflow — printed in alternating Habanero Yellow and Molten Coral directly on the Ghost Pepper Purple panel. The labels beneath each number are tiny Permanent Marker in Lava Cream, creating a violent scale contrast that makes the numbers feel like graffiti stencils on a wall. This is unmistakably Memphis: bold graphic type used as image, flat color doing all the heavy lifting, zero decoration needed because the type IS the decoration. The numbers count up from zero as the section enters the viewport — a scroll-triggered counting animation — making the arrival of each stat feel like a small celebration.

**Signature Motion Moment:** As Section 4 scrolls into view, each of the four oversized numerals counts up from 0 to its final value in a staggered sequence — the first number starts counting, then a beat later the second joins, then the third, then the fourth — so the purple panel feels like it's erupting with data. The counting motion is fast and snappy (each number reaches its final value in about one second), and when each number lands, it gives a brief elastic bounce — scaling up slightly past its final size then settling back — echoing the Memphis energy of the whole page.

### Color & Surface Logic Across the Page
- Section 1: Lava Cream background with Molten Coral headline fill, Ghost Pepper Purple for the eyebrow pill, Confetti Pink and Habanero Yellow Memphis shapes scattered across the surface.
- Section 2: Habanero Yellow full-bleed background. Cards are Lava Cream with Smoke Ring Black text and Molten Coral icon fills.
- Section 3: Lava Cream background. Product card backgrounds cycle: Molten Coral, Jalapeño Teal, Ghost Pepper Purple, Sauce Bottle Green — each card is a saturated block with Lava Cream or white text.
- Section 4: Ghost Pepper Purple full-bleed. Numerals in alternating Habanero Yellow and Molten Coral. Label text in Lava Cream via Permanent Marker.
- Section 5: Molten Coral full-bleed. Headline in Habanero Yellow. Subhead in Lava Cream. CTAs: one Ghost Pepper Purple fill with Lava Cream text, one Lava Cream fill with Smoke Ring Black text.

### Typographic Hierarchy
- H1 (Hero): Boogaloo, 88–100px, all-caps, Molten Coral fill on Lava Cream. Tight tracking. Feels shouted.
- H2 (Section headlines): Boogaloo, 52–64px, sentence case except Section 5 which is all-caps. Color varies by section surface.
- H3 (Card/item titles): Boogaloo, 36–40px, sentence case.
- Eyebrow labels: Permanent Marker, 12–14px, loose tracking, in pill backgrounds.
- Body / descriptions: Nunito, 16–18px, 1.7 line-height, 400 weight for card descriptions, 600 semi-bold for section subheadlines.
- Stat numerals (Section 4): Boogaloo, 120–160px, treated as graphic objects.

### Memphis Visual Cues — Applied at Full Amplitude
Memphis shapes are NOT tucked into corners. In the hero, abstract squiggles, zigzag lines, confetti triangles, and dot clusters are scattered across the full surface at varying scales — some behind the headline, some overlapping the mascot illustration's edges, some bleeding off the viewport edge. In Section 5, confetti shapes (triangles, circles, squiggles) fall across the coral panel at multiple depths, some at 60% opacity to create layering. The mascot illustration in the hero overflows its container, crossing into the section below — a deliberate Memphis overlap that refuses to stay inside its box.

### Density & Whitespace Logic
The page alternates between dense/graphic sections (Hero, Stats, CTA Close) and slightly more breathable sections (Feature Grid cards, Product Grid cards). Even the "breathable" sections are energetic — the breathing room is used for bold color blocks, not empty space. No section feels like a rest; each feels like a different flavor of loud.

### Motion Design — Full Arc

**On-Load Arc (Hero):**
1. The Habanero Yellow and Confetti Pink Memphis background shapes fade and slide in from slightly off-position simultaneously as the page loads — a quick 300ms scatter-settle.
2. A beat after the shapes settle, the eyebrow pill pops in with a quick scale-from-zero bounce.
3. The H1 headline slams in from slightly below — a fast upward slide with a tiny elastic overshoot — landing hard like a stamp.
4. A beat after the headline lands, the subheadline fades up from below.
5. A beat after the subhead, the two CTA buttons slide in from the left with a short stagger between them.
6. The mascot illustration drifts in from the right edge — a smooth slide-in that arrives slightly after the CTAs — and then begins a slow, continuous ambient float (gentle up-down drift on a 4-second loop, very subtle, as if the chili is breathing).
7. The Memphis background shapes continue a very slow, almost imperceptible parallax drift as the user scrolls — shapes in the "foreground" move slightly faster than those in the "background."

**Scroll-Triggered Reveals:**
- Section 2 (Feature Grid): The section headline slides up and fades in as the section enters the viewport. The three cards stagger in from below — left card first, then center (which is also pushed up vertically), then right — each with a quick upward slide and fade, arriving about half a beat apart.
- Section 3 (Product Grid): Cards scale in from 95% to 100% with a fade, staggered in reading order (top-left → top-right → bottom-left → bottom-right), each arriving a beat after the previous.
- Section 4 (Stats): The Ghost Pepper Purple panel fades in as a full-bleed color wash, then the four stat numerals count up from zero in a staggered sequence — first number starts, then a beat later the second joins, and so on. Each number lands with a brief elastic bounce. This is the **signature motion moment**.
- Section 5 (CTA Close): The confetti shapes scatter across the coral panel as it enters the viewport — a quick burst-and-settle. The headline scales up from 90% with a fade. CTAs slide up staggered.

**Hover & Focus Affordances:**
- Hero CTAs: On hover, the primary CTA (Shop the Sauces) lifts 4px with a shadow deepening and its background shifts one shade darker (coral darkens). The secondary CTA border brightens. Both respond to keyboard focus with a visible outline in Habanero Yellow.
- Feature Grid cards: On hover, the card lifts 6px, shadow grows, and the icon scales up to 110% with a quick 150ms ease. The card border (Smoke Ring Black, 2px) thickens to 3px.
- Product cards: On hover, the card scales to 102%, the product title shifts to Habanero Yellow (on dark card backgrounds) or Molten Coral (on light ones), and a "View Sauce →" text link fades in at the bottom of the card.
- CTA Close buttons: On hover, the Ghost Pepper Purple button gains a Habanero Yellow border and the text shifts to Habanero Yellow. The Lava Cream button gains a Smoke Ring Black border.
- All interactive elements have a visible focus ring in Habanero Yellow for keyboard navigation.

**Ambient Looped Motion:**
- Hero mascot illustration: slow, continuous up-down float on a 4-second loop.
- Memphis background shapes in the hero: extremely slow rotation drift (some shapes rotate 1–2 degrees over 8 seconds and back) — barely perceptible but adds life.
- Section 5 CTA close: the primary "Shop Now" button has a slow pulsing glow — a soft Habanero Yellow halo that breathes in and out on a 2.5-second loop — making it feel like it's beckoning.
- A marquee strip between Section 2 and Section 3: a continuous left-scrolling ticker of alternating sauce names and flame emoji, rendered in Boogaloo on a Jalapeño Teal strip — scrolls at a steady, hypnotic pace. This is a structural Memphis device, not decoration.

### Responsive Behavior
- **Desktop (1280px+):** All layouts as described. Hero is full-viewport-height. Product grid is 2×2. Stats are four columns.
- **Tablet (768–1279px):** Hero text stack and mascot stack vertically (text above, illustration below, still overflowing). Feature grid becomes a 3-column row but cards are narrower. Product grid stays 2×2. Stats become 2×2.
- **Mobile (< 768px):** Hero is single-column, mascot illustration sits below the text stack and is cropped to show the face/upper body only. Feature grid stacks to a single column. Product grid stacks to a single column with full-width cards. Stats stack 2×2. CTA close stacks CTAs vertically. Marquee strip persists at all breakpoints. Memphis shapes scale down but remain visible — never hidden.

### Fit Within Shared Design System
This page uses all eight palette colors expressively — not just as accent touches. Boogaloo dominates at display scale. Nunito handles all body copy. Permanent Marker appears on eyebrow pills and stat labels only — never at heading scale. The mascot illustration and Memphis icon set introduced here establish visual motifs that echo across the Products and Story pages. The marquee strip device will recur on the Products page, creating cross-page rhythm.
---

content.content:
1	PAGE INSTR:
2	## Products Page — Full Visual Design Direction
3	
4	### Page Role & Goal
5	This is the full product catalog for Lava Mouth — a scrolling celebration of six small-batch hot sauces, each treated as a distinct personality rather than a SKU. The page must feel like walking through a loud, joyful market stall where every bottle is calling for attention. The Memphis Playful aesthetic is deployed at full amplitude: confetti shapes, bold color blocks, patterned surfaces, and display typography doing structural work, not just decorative work.
6	
7	---
8	
9	### Section Sequence & Rhythm
10	
11	**Section 1 — Page Header:** Dense, loud, pattern-saturated arrival. Full-bleed Memphis tile pattern behind a left-aligned masthead-style type treatment. High energy, maximum graphic density. No whitespace padding relief — the pattern fills edge to edge.
12	
13	**Section 2 — Product Grid:** The page's longest and most structurally complex section. A staggered, asymmetric card grid where each sauce card has a distinct dominant color pulled from the palette. Cards are not identical columns — they vary in vertical offset and size weight to feel like a hand-arranged market display. This is the densest content section.
14	
15	**Section 3 — Heat Comparison:** A deliberate shift in rhythm — wider breathing room, a single bold horizontal heat-scale chart dominates the layout. This is the page's **signature moment** (described below). The section is structured as a side-tabbed layout: the five heat tiers stack vertically on the left as a labeled index, while the chart and sauce names occupy the right two-thirds. Moderately sparse compared to Section 2.
16	
17	**Section 4 — Testimonials:** Full-bleed Ghost Pepper Purple panel. Three testimonial quotes arranged in an off-axis staggered layout — not identical card columns. The section softens the energy slightly with genuine human voice but keeps the Memphis graphic energy alive through bold typographic pull quotes.
18	
19	**Section 5 — CTA Close:** A punchy, asymmetric close on a Habanero Yellow background. Oversized display headline, two CTA buttons, and a burst of confetti shapes overlapping the panel boundary. Short, urgent, fun.
20	
21	---
22	
23	### Signature Moment
24	
25	**Named: "The Flame Scale Takeover" — Section 3, Heat Comparison.**
26	
27	The heat scale chart (a Memphis-illustrated horizontal gradient bar from Habanero Yellow through Molten Coral to a deep red-black) is rendered at oversized, page-dominating width — it bleeds past the text column and nearly reaches the page edge on both sides, breaking the section's grid containment. The five flame-tier labels are set in Boogaloo at 36px, stacked vertically on the left as a bold index column in alternating Jalapeño Teal and Molten Coral fills. The chart bar itself is thick — approximately 80–100px tall — with flame icons at each tier node rendered as oversized Memphis graphic shapes (not emoji, not icons — bold flat-color illustrated flames in the brand palette). The sauce name for each tier is annotated in Permanent Marker directly on or just below the bar at each node, like a hand-stamped label. This move is unmistakably Memphis: it treats a data visualization as a graphic design object, uses color and scale as structural tools, and turns a utilitarian comparison into a page-defining visual moment. No other aesthetic would produce this exact gesture.
28	
29	---
30	
31	### Signature Motion Moment
32	
33	**Named: "The Flame Bar Ignition" — Section 3.**
34	
35	When the heat scale section scrolls into view, the gradient bar animates from left to right as if being drawn or filled in real time — starting at the cool yellow end and "burning" across to the deep red extreme over approximately 1.2 seconds. Each flame icon at the five tier nodes pops in sequentially, one beat apart, with a brief upward bounce (scale from 0.5 to 1.1 then settle to 1.0) timed to the bar's fill reaching that node. The tier labels on the left index slide in from the left, staggered one after another. This motion is tied directly to the signature visual moment and reinforces the heat-progression narrative — the animation tells the story of escalating heat before the visitor reads a word.
36	
37	---
38	
39	### Color & Surface Usage Across the Page
40	
41	- **Section 1 (Header):** Lava Cream background with the Memphis tile pattern rendered in Habanero Yellow, Confetti Pink, Jalapeño Teal, and Smoke Ring Black line-work. Headline in Molten Coral on the cream/pattern surface. Eyebrow pill in Confetti Pink.
42	- **Section 2 (Grid):** Lava Cream page background. Each product card has its own dominant background color pulled from the palette in rotation: Serrano Verde → Jalapeño Teal card; Smoky Diablo → Smoke Ring Black card; Mango Inferno → Habanero Yellow card; Pineapple Fury → Confetti Pink card; Ghost Town → Ghost Pepper Purple card; Carolina Reaper's Edge → Molten Coral card. Headline text on dark cards in Lava Cream or Habanero Yellow; on light cards in Smoke Ring Black. Section eyebrow and headline in Smoke Ring Black on Lava Cream above the grid.
43	- **Section 3 (Comparison):** Lava Cream background. The heat bar is the color hero — yellow to coral gradient. Left index column text alternates Jalapeño Teal and Molten Coral fills. Permanent Marker annotations in Smoke Ring Black on the bar.
44	- **Section 4 (Testimonials):** Full-bleed Ghost Pepper Purple background. Quote text in Lava Cream. Attribution in Habanero Yellow. Decorative squiggles and confetti dots in Confetti Pink and Molten Coral scattered around the panel.
45	- **Section 5 (CTA):** Full-bleed Habanero Yellow background. Headline in Smoke Ring Black (maximum contrast). Primary CTA button in Molten Coral with Lava Cream text; secondary CTA in Smoke Ring Black with Lava Cream text. Confetti shapes in Ghost Pepper Purple and Jalapeño Teal overlapping the top and bottom edges of the panel.
46	
47	---
48	
49	### Typographic Hierarchy & Expressive Moves
50	
51	- **Boogaloo** at 80–100px (H1 equivalent) for the page header headline. At 52–64px for section headlines in Sections 2 and 3. At 36–42px for product card titles and heat-tier labels. All-caps for the page header and CTA headline; sentence case for product card titles and comparison tiers.
52	- **Nunito** at 16–18px, semi-bold 600 for product descriptions and body copy in the comparison section. Regular 400 for testimonial quote text.
53	- **Permanent Marker** at 11–14px for eyebrow labels (pill backgrounds in Confetti Pink), heat-scale bar annotations, and the "Ready to Commit?" eyebrow in Section 5. Loose letter-spacing. Never at heading scale.
54	- The product card titles in Section 2 use Boogaloo with color fills matching the card's palette role — e.g., Habanero Yellow title on the Ghost Pepper Purple Ghost Town card, Smoke Ring Black title on the Habanero Yellow Mango Inferno card.
55	- The CTA headline in Section 5 ("Your Kitchen Needs This") is set at 80px Boogaloo, all-caps, in Smoke Ring Black — the largest type on the page after the header, and deliberately off-center aligned to the left third of the panel.
56	
57	---
58	
59	### Density & Whitespace Logic
60	
61	The page follows a deliberate dense → dense → airy → full-bleed → punchy rhythm:
62	- Section 1: Dense (pattern-saturated, minimal padding)
63	- Section 2: Dense (six cards, staggered grid, rich metadata)
64	- Section 3: Moderate breathing room (chart dominates, generous vertical padding around the bar)
65	- Section 4: Full-bleed color block (contained density within the purple panel, but the panel itself is a relief from the grid)
66	- Section 5: Short and punchy (minimal copy, maximum type scale, fast exit)
67	
68	---
69	
70	### Motion Design — Full Page Arc
71	
72	**On-load arc (Section 1):**
73	The Memphis tile pattern fades in first as the page loads, appearing over about 0.4 seconds. The eyebrow pill slides down from slightly above its resting position. The main headline ("Every Sauce Has a Story") scales up from 90% to 100% and fades in — arriving bold and settled. The subheadline follows a beat later with a gentle upward slide.
74	
75	**Scroll-triggered reveals:**
76	- Section 2: Each product card slides up and fades in as the grid enters the viewport, staggered left-to-right, top row first then bottom row, with approximately a half-beat between each card. Children (title, description, metadata tags) do not animate separately — the card as a unit is the reveal.
77	- Section 3: The "Flame Bar Ignition" signature motion (described above) triggers when the chart enters the viewport.
78	- Section 4: The full purple panel fades in as a block. The three testimonial quotes then slide up from below in sequence, one beat apart.
79	- Section 5: The confetti shapes scatter in from the top and bottom edges (scale from 0 to 1) as the CTA panel enters view. The headline and buttons follow immediately after.
80	
81	**Hover & focus affordances:**
82	- Product cards (Section 2): On hover, the card lifts 6px with a deepened drop shadow (Smoke Ring Black at 20% opacity, larger spread). The card's dominant background color lightens by about 10% (achieved via a semi-transparent white overlay). The "Find a Stockist" CTA button at the bottom of the grid shifts from a Molten Coral fill to a Ghost Pepper Purple fill on hover, with Lava Cream text maintained.
83	- Heat tier rows (Section 3): On hover, the hovered tier row highlights with a Habanero Yellow left border (4px) and the sauce name annotation on the bar pulses briefly (quick scale to 1.05 and back).
84	- Testimonial cards (Section 4): Subtle — the card background lightens from Ghost Pepper Purple to a slightly lighter purple tint on hover, and the attribution text shifts from Habanero Yellow to Lava Cream.
85	- CTA buttons (Section 5): Primary button lifts 4px with a Smoke Ring Black shadow on hover. Secondary button inverts fill and text color on hover.
86	
87	**Ambient looped motion:**
88	- The Memphis tile pattern in Section 1 very slowly drifts — the entire pattern translates diagonally (down-right) at a glacial pace, completing one tile-width of movement over about 12 seconds, then looping seamlessly. This creates a living, breathing header surface.
89	- A horizontal marquee strip runs between Section 2 and Section 3 — a narrow Jalapeño Teal band carrying repeating text in Permanent Marker: "MILD · MEDIUM · HOT · EXTRA HOT · EXTREME · MILD · MEDIUM · HOT ·" scrolling left continuously at a steady, hypnotic pace. This acts as both a visual divider and an ambient motion element.
90	- The confetti shapes in Section 5 have a slow ambient float — each shape drifts up and down independently on a gentle sine-wave cycle (different phases per shape), giving the CTA panel a lively, celebratory energy.
91	
92	---
93	
94	### Responsive Behavior
95	
96	- **Desktop (≥1280px):** Full staggered grid in Section 2 (3 columns, offset rows). Heat chart at full bleed width. Side-tabbed layout in Section 3.
97	- **Tablet (768–1279px):** Section 2 grid collapses to 2 columns, still staggered. Section 3 switches from side-tab to stacked (index above chart). Testimonials in Section 4 stack vertically.
98	- **Mobile (<768px):** Section 2 is a single-column scroll of cards, each full-width. The heat chart in Section 3 scales down but remains the dominant element; the tier index stacks above it. All display type scales down proportionally (H1 to ~52px, H2 to ~36px). The marquee strip between sections remains full-width and scrolling. Confetti shapes in Section 5 reduce in quantity to avoid clutter.
99	
100	---
101	
102	### Fit Within Shared Design System
103	
104	This page uses all eight palette colors across its five sections — no color is left idle. The typographic trio (Boogaloo, Nunito, Permanent Marker) is deployed at every scale level appropriate to each. The Memphis visual cues (patterned backgrounds, confetti shapes, squiggles, bright blocks) are structural devices here — the pattern is the header background, the color blocks are the card identities, the confetti shapes are the CTA's decorative architecture. The page is unmistakably Lava Mouth: loud, joyful, irreverent, and warm — with every visual decision traceable to the Memphis Playful aesthetic and the Storytelling Scroll layout's sequential, narrative momentum.
105	===
106	
107	SECTION ID: products-section-1
108	**Section 1 — Page Header (products-section-1)**
109

111	
112	**Background pattern asset:** The repeating Memphis tile pattern (tiny chili peppers, flame shapes, zigzag lines, polka dots) is rendered behind all content. The tile is dense and energetic. Colors in the pattern: Habanero Yellow shapes, Confetti Pink dots, Jalapeño Teal zigzags, and Smoke Ring Black line-work on a Lava Cream base tile. The pattern animates with a slow ambient drift — the entire tile translates diagonally (down and to the right) over 12 seconds, completing exactly one tile-unit of travel before looping seamlessly.
